transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm explaining this right, but what brings me in is... well, I just can't seem to keep my work in order anymore. 

I work down at the dry cleaner's, and... it's a little embarrassing to admit, but the tickets, and the receipts, and my workshop notes—they all just sort of get piled together with the customer jobs. I try my best to keep it neat, I really do, but it just builds up until I... I honestly don't know what to handle first. I feel terrible about it, letting it get like that. Am I making sense? I hope that's an okay thing to bring up here.
Did you have similar problems with organization or attention when you were a child, before age 12?

Oh, um... yes, I suppose I did. I hope it's alright to go back that far. 

Even in grade school... well, my teachers were always very sweet, and they told my mother I was a bright girl, which was nice of them to say. But... they also said I was a bit, um, scattered. I never ever wanted to be a bother to anyone, but I guess I had a bad habit of talking out of turn. And my school papers would just sort of disappear on me, or I'd need extra reminders to finish my assignments. 

I really tried to be a good student, I promise, it's just... I've always been a little clumsy with keeping things straight. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question the right way.
Do you often feel restless or like you need to be moving around?

Oh... um, well, I don't think so? I hope it's okay to say that. I mean, I'm on my feet almost all day at the shop, running back and forth to the racks and the presses, so I guess I stay pretty busy anyway. But I don't really feel... restless, like I *have* to be moving. 

Usually, when I finally get to sit down at home, I'm just happy to rest my feet. I haven't really noticed feeling jittery or anything like that. I hope I'm understanding your question right... is that what you meant?
Do you often act before thinking, such as interrupting people or blurting things out?

Oh, um... well, I really try my best to be polite, I promise. I would never want anyone to think I was being rude on purpose. But... I guess sometimes I do get a little too eager to help? 

Like, if a customer is at the counter, or my daughter is talking to me, or even if I'm talking to the trainer at work... I sometimes just jump right in with an answer before they've even finished asking their question. I just want to be helpful and get them what they need quickly, you know? But then... well, it's a little embarrassing, but sometimes I find out I answered the complete wrong thing because I didn't wait to hear the end of the sentence. 

I always feel just awful when it happens, and I apologize right away. I hope that doesn't make me sound terrible... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
When you were younger, did you often fidget, squirm, or have trouble sitting still?

Oh, goodness... when I was younger? Um... well, I suppose I wasn't the best at sitting perfectly still, but I wasn't... I mean, I wasn't a bad child or anything. I hope you don't think I was a troublemaker. 

I remember my mother used to gently remind me to stop tapping my foot under the dinner table, or she'd tell me to stop playing with the hem of my skirt during church. I guess I just always had a little extra energy, you know? But I always tried to be quiet about it so I wouldn't bother anyone. 

I don't think I was ever really squirming all over the place, just... maybe a little wiggly sometimes? I hope that's an okay answer. Does that sound like what you were looking for?
Did a teacher, parent, or doctor ever say you had ADHD or a similar attention problem when you were a child?

Oh, um... well, nobody ever used that exact word, ADHD, I don't think. Back then, they didn't really talk about things like that the way they do now, especially not for girls. I hope it's alright if I explain it like this... 

I mean, my teachers always said very nice things about me! They always told my mother I was a bright girl, which was sweet of them. But... well, they did also mention that I could be a little, um, scattered? 

Like, they'd say I had a habit of talking out of turn sometimes—just because I was excited to participate, really!—and I might have misplaced a paper or two. And they said I sometimes needed a few extra gentle reminders to get my assignments finished. But they didn't mean it in a bad way, I don't think. Just that I was a bit disorganized. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a terrible student... is that the sort of thing you meant?
Before age 12, did you have ongoing trouble paying attention in class?

Oh, um... paying attention in class? Well, I really did try my best to be a good student, I promise. I always wanted to do well and make my teachers happy. 

I don't think I had... well, I wouldn't call it *trouble*, exactly. I mean, I wasn't falling asleep or ignoring the teacher on purpose! Sometimes, I suppose, if the lesson was a little dry, my mind might wander just a tiny bit. Like, I might start thinking about what we were having for dinner, or looking out the window for a moment. But I always tried to snap right back to it as soon as I realized. 

I hope that doesn't make it sound like I didn't care about school. I really did! Do you think that's normal for a little girl, just daydreaming a little bit here and there?
Were these attention and organization problems present before you were 12 years old?

Oh, um... yes, I suppose they were. Like I mentioned before, even back in grade school, my teachers would tell my mother that I was a bright girl... but they did say I was a little scattered. 

I really didn't mean to be a bother, but I guess I was always talking out of turn a bit, or, you know, losing my papers here and there. And I did need those gentle reminders to finish my work. But that was all before I was 12, yes. I hope it's okay that I brought that up again... I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right. Am I doing okay?
Do these attention and organization problems also happen outside of work, such as at home?

Oh, um... well, yes, I suppose they do happen outside of work, too. I really try my best to keep everything running smoothly everywhere, I promise. 

At the dry cleaners where I work, well... sometimes things get a little mixed up. Like, a few orders might have been a tiny bit late, or there was a little confusion with the billing. And I guess there have been a few, um, tense moments with the staff and customers because of it. I always feel so terrible when that happens, because I really do want everyone to be happy! 

And, um, at church... well, I used to help lead some of the planning for our events. I love being involved and helping out! But... I actually decided to step back from that recently. I think maybe some people were getting a little frustrated with me because I was having trouble keeping all the details straight. I just didn't want to be a burden to anyone, you know? 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm completely irresponsible... I really do try very hard. Does that make sense, what I just explained?
Do these attention and organization problems usually cause real difficulties in your daily life?

Oh, um... well, I suppose they do cause some bumps in the road, yes. I really try not to let it affect things too much, but... like I mentioned about the dry cleaners, we've had those late orders and the billing mix-ups. And it has caused some tense moments with the staff and the customers. I hate that it happens because I want everyone to have a good experience! 

And with church, stepping back from the event planning... that was mostly because I could tell people were getting a little frustrated with me. I just didn't want to cause any more trouble or make things harder for the group. I really hope I'm not making a mess of things... I'm trying my absolute best to keep up. Do you think it's okay that I stepped back from the church planning to try and fix things?
As a child, did you have trouble learning to read?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I actually always liked reading when I was little. I mean, maybe I wasn't the absolute fastest reader in the class, but I didn't have any real trouble learning. I always tried very hard to pay attention during reading time. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just don't remember it being a problem for me.
Have you ever had ongoing difficulty learning to read, such as recognizing words, sounding them out, or understanding what you read?

Oh, um... no, I haven't really had any trouble like that. I read just fine, honestly. I try to read carefully so I understand everything... I don't have any problems sounding words out or anything. I mean, sometimes if I'm tired I might have to read a sentence twice, but that's normal, right? I really do try to make sure I understand what I'm reading. Is that what you were asking about?
Did you ever have ongoing trouble with spelling?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I've always been pretty okay at spelling, actually. I mean, I always try to double-check my notes at the dry cleaners to make sure everything looks nice and professional for the customers, but I don't remember ever having any real trouble with it in school or anything. I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Have you ever had ongoing difficulty with reading, such as recognizing words or sounding them out?

Oh, um... I think you might have asked me something similar just a minute ago? I hope I didn't give you the wrong impression earlier! But no, I really haven't ever had trouble recognizing words or anything like that. 

I have to read the tiny care labels and the customer tickets at the shop all day, and I do just fine with it. I always try to be very careful with reading them so I don't ruin anyone's nice clothes... Am I answering that right for you? I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
When you were learning to read as a child, did letters or words ever seem to move around or flip on the page?

Oh, no, nothing like that. I've never seen letters moving around or flipping or anything strange like that. I was a pretty normal reader as a kid, I think. I mean, I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. I never had any kind of vision or reading problems like that, honestly. Does that make sense?
Did you have trouble with math when you were a child?

Oh, um... math? No, I don't think I struggled with that. Well, I wasn't exactly at the top of the class or anything, but I did okay! I still do all the cash register stuff at the shop, counting out change and everything, and I never really mess that up. So I think my math skills have always been pretty normal. 

I hope it's alright that I keep saying no to these? I really want to be helpful and do this right, I just... I don't want to make up problems I didn't have. Is this still giving you what you need to know?
When you were a child, did you ever have trouble sounding out words while reading?

Oh, um... I think we might have just touched on this one, didn't we? I'm so sorry, I hope I didn't give you a confusing answer the first time! But no, sounding out words was always okay for me back then. I really didn't have any trouble with that part of school. 

I'm sorry if I'm not giving you much to work with here... I promise I'm just trying to be completely honest with you so you get the right picture. Is it okay that I keep saying no to the reading questions? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and doing this right for you.
